registration.notes: Oklahoma does not require general charitable solicitation registration. Only specific categories (veterans, law enforcement telephone solicitors) must register.

annualFiling.notes: Must file annual certificate with registered agent and address updates

salesTax.notes: 501(c)(3) organizations may apply for sales tax exemption

propertyTax.notes: Property used exclusively for charitable purposes may be exempt

incomeTax.notes: Oklahoma conforms to federal tax-exempt status for qualifying organizations

form990.notes: Oklahoma does not require nonprofits to file copies of Form 990 with any state agency (unlike NY or CA)

auditRequirements.notes: No state-mandated audit threshold for nonprofits. Board discretion.

religiousExemptions.notes: Religious organizations are fully exempt from registration and most state reporting

oklahomaCity.solicitation: Permit may be required for door-to-door solicitation
oklahomaCity.events: Special event permits through city clerk
oklahomaCity.notes: Check with OKC City Clerk for specific event requirements

tulsa.solicitation: Similar to OKC — local permit may apply
tulsa.events: Parks and public space events require Tulsa Parks Department permit
tulsa.notes: Food-related events need Tulsa Health Department approval

recentUpdates.description: HB 4752 — Property tax exemption expansion for charitable gift distribution organizations (passed House, awaiting Senate)
recentUpdates.impact: If passed, expands property tax exemptions for nonprofits distributing gifts/grants

complianceNotes: Oklahoma is one of the most nonprofit-friendly states — minimal registration requirements
No state charitable solicitation registration for most nonprofits
Annual certificate with Secretary of State is the primary state obligation
Federal Form 990 filing remains required regardless of state rules
